name: PS5MC
description: PS5MC, an unofficial port of the Kodi 22 media center for PS5, with a 4K GPU interface, hardware H.264, HEVC and VP9 decoding and HDR output.
author: VivaLaVent
release_notes:
PS5MC 1.2
Kodi with the PS5 as a first-class platform, in two builds. Each comes as a single-file .exfat image (recommended) or a .zip of the title folder:
- build · Kodi · title ID · home screen name · files
- Kodi 22 · 22.0 RC1 (Piers) · PPSA99420 · PS5MC (Kodi 22) · PS5MC-1.2-kodi22-PPSA99420.exfat or .zip
- Kodi 21 · 21.3 (Omega) · PPSA99421 · PS5MC (Kodi 21) · PS5MC-1.2-kodi21-PPSA99421.exfat or .zip

Pick 22 unless an add-on or skin you need only works on 21 (for example skins that need Skin Shortcuts v2, such as Aeon Nox or Arctic Zephyr). The two keep separate data and can be installed side by side.

Changes since 1.1
Video
- Three fixes listed in the 1.1 notes were missing from the 1.1 builds. They are in 1.2:
- 4K HEVC whose own stream headers differ from its container's (seen with x265 MKV encodes) was refused by the hardware decoder and fell back to software decoding, which is choppy at 4K. It now plays in hardware.
- HEVC coded in tiles, which the PS5's decoder does not support, goes straight to software decoding instead of failing in hardware first.
- Dolby Vision profile 7/8: the Dolby Vision layers are removed before the hardware decoder sees them, so playback starts without a failed first attempt.

Kodi 21 build
- The skin now displays completely. In 1.1 the Kodi 21 build showed black backgrounds and no icons, buttons or focus highlights: its images used a pixel format the PS5's graphics driver does not accept, and its skin textures were packed in Kodi 22's format, which Kodi 21 cannot read.

Network
- A network-share account that the server has locked out (too many wrong passwords) is now recognised as locked. Kodi no longer asks for the password again and retries, which kept the account locked; the log says so plainly.

System
- The Kodi 22 build is now called PS5MC (Kodi 22) on the home screen, and each build has its own boot splash.
- Each release carries its version number, so stores and updaters can offer it as an update.
- kodi-reset and kodi-uninstall only touch the build they run in. In 1.1 they also erased the other build's library.
- Switch files (kodi-debug, kodi-reset, kodi-uninstall) also work from the build's data folder, /data/ps5mc/kodi22 or /data/ps5mc/kodi21, so they work with the .exfat install too.
- Logs name the exact build, for bug reports.
- Under the hood: development diagnostics removed, per-frame video work streamlined.

Releases
- New: a single-file .exfat image per build.
- Each title folder ships a MANIFEST.sha256 to check that a copy is complete.

Install
ShadowMountPlus 1.7beta4 or later is needed for the .exfat image, and it gives Kodi the /data folder where it keeps its library and settings.
- .exfat (recommended), a single file. Copy it to /data/homebrew/. One file can't partially transfer, so it avoids the dropped-file problems a folder copy over FTP can have.
- .zip, the title folder. Extract it into /data/homebrew/ (creates PPSA99420/ or PPSA99421/), replacing the whole folder. If you copy with FileZilla, set Settings > Transfers > File exists action to Overwrite, delete any old folder first, and check that the Failed transfers tab is empty. Run sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256 in the folder to confirm the copy is complete.

Use one format per build: when switching between the folder and the image, delete the other one first.

Coming from 1.1: same title IDs and data folders, so settings, library and add-ons carry over. The Kodi 22 build also carries over from kodi-ps5 0.9.

Known issues
- Intermittent black screen on some 4K HDR films (sound plays, the menus are not visible; one report is a letterboxed 3840x2076 film). Under investigation: if it happens, please send a log captured with kodi-debug on, and say whether the film is letterboxed.
- Dolby Vision profile 5 files show the wrong colours (a green and purple tint): that profile has no HDR10 layer and needs per-frame Dolby Vision processing, not yet done. Profiles 7 and 8 play their HDR10 picture.
